newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel team heading for Comoro Islands.
newsitem.headline: Israel team heading for Comoro Islands.

text.p: Israel is sending a team to get information on eight of its nationals who were on a hijacked Ethiopian plane that crashed near the Comoro Islands, a spokesman said on Saturday.
Israel does not have diplomatic ties with Comoro Islands.

Foreign ministry spokesman Danny Shek said Israel has not yet obtained permission for its plane to land at Comoro Islands but that the team would fly on a small plane and would make a stopover at an unnamed airport where further consultations would be held on whether to continue on to the islands.

"It will leave in two hours, a little more, and it will have a medical staff (and)...a technical staff whose primary job will be to establish a direct and independent link to there and the deputy head of the foreign ministry for African affairs," Shek told Israel Radio. The plane was to leave around 2200 GMT.
"To our great regret there is still at the moment no possibility like that. We still have not succeeded in establishing direct communications," he said.

An Israeli embassy official in Ethiopia, Meir Yitzhaki, told Israel's army radio: "We know there were eight Israelis on the plane." The foreign ministry later confirmed the Israelis were four employees of Israel Aircraft Industries, two businessmen and two students.

The Israeli army later said it would have personnel on the team: "In the plane...there are also army medical crews and an army rabbinate crew. This flight's mission is to aid and to report on further needs".

At least 50 people were killed when the hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 with 175 passengers and crew aboard crashed into the sea. Airline officials said the plane had tried to make an emergency landing after running out of fuel.
